Session · What happened (August 17)
The session focused on refining the Team Intelligence Agent's capabilities, designing a robust knowledge base, and structuring the RAG pipeline into deployable services. Key discussions revolved around defining "intelligence" for the agent, establishing clear system boundaries, and planning for the deployment of components like the vector store and retrieval services.

Technical concepts discussed
*   **Team Intelligence Agent Capabilities**: Discussion on what "intelligence" means for the agent, moving beyond simple RAG to infer and evaluate, and the need for a locked persona and rules for generating comprehensive reports [17 August 2026, Page 2-4 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Knowledge Base Design**: Exploration of what information the knowledge base should store (people, roles, tasks, projects, decisions, assignments, terminology, events, facts) and how it should be structured, including the concept of a "training profile" for each team member [17 August 2026, Page 1-3 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **System Boundaries and Architecture**: Detailed breakdown of the RAG pipeline into three distinct systems: the vector store (System 1), the main RAG/retrieval service (System 2), and the unified evaluation system (System 3). Emphasis on making the re-ranker a separate, reusable module [17 August 2026, Page 6-9 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **FastAPI for Service Wrapping**: The approach to wrap the three core systems (vector store, retrieval, evaluation) as FastAPI services for deployment and API calls [17 August 2026, Page 10-11 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Quadrant Cloud Deployment**: Practical steps for creating a Quadrant cluster, obtaining API keys and endpoints, and understanding its features for vector storage and retrieval [17 August 2026, Page 14-17 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Normalization Layer**: The need for a generic normalization solution for transcripts, moving away from hardcoded patterns to an agent-based capability [17 August 2026, Page 1 — Siddharth Saminathan].

Assignments and actions
*   **System Owner**:
    *   **Refine Team Intelligence Agent Capabilities**: Rework the capabilities of the Team Intelligence Agent to align with the definition of "intelligence" discussed, focusing on inference and evaluation rather than just retrieval. This includes locking the agent's persona and defining a set of rules [17 August 2026, Page 4 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   **Design Knowledge Base (V1)**: Develop the first version of the knowledge base design, including a JSON schema for the "training profile" that captures facts and observable events for each team member. This profile should include name, thinking style, assigned tasks, and evaluation scores [17 August 2026, Page 2-4 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   **Build Mentor and Manager Agents**: Prioritize building the mentor and manager agents, ensuring they are working and demonstrate proper tool calls, roles, and personas. Focus on harness engineering, context engineering, and prompt engineering [17 August 2026, Page 13-14 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   **Develop Generic Normalizer**: Transform the existing hardcoded normalizer into a generic solution that can identify patterns and label them using an agent-based capability, rather than manual hardcoding [17 August 2026, Page 1 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   **Evaluate Normalizer Performance**: Test the generic normalizer with today's morning transcript to evaluate its performance and ensure it is doing a good job [17 August 2026, Page 1-2 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   **Connect to GitHub MCP**: Configure the Team Intelligence Agent to connect to GitHub MCP using tokens from all three team members to read code and information from their respective GitHub repositories [17 August 2026, Page 12-13 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   **Show Working Agents and Knowledge Base Design**: Present working mentor and manager agents, along with the design of the knowledge base, including whether it's a combination of Postgres and Quadrant, or only one, and what each component represents [17 August 2026, Page 17 — Siddharth Saminathan].

Decisions
*   **Team Intelligence Agent Persona**: The Team Intelligence Agent must have one locked persona with a defined set of rules [17 August 2026, Page 2 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **RAG Pipeline Architecture**: The RAG pipeline will be structured into three main systems: Vector Store (System 1), Main RAG/Retrieval Service (System 2), and Unified Evaluation System (System 3) [17 August 2026, Page 7 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Re-ranker as Separate Module**: The re-ranker component within the retrieval service must be made a separate, reusable module to allow for flexible integration across different experiments [17 August 2026, Page 8 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Prompt Management**: Prompts should be externalized into a separate prompt builder service instead of being hardcoded in Python files to protect core logic [17 August 2026, Page 9 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Shared GitHub Repo for Documents**: A shared GitHub repository will be created for documents, and the systems will connect to this repo instead of MCP for document retrieval [17 August 2026, Page 12-13 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Knowledge Base Update Mechanism**: The knowledge base, specifically the training profile, should be updated daily via a job, with facts remaining constant and observed events being mutable [17 August 2026, Page 2-3 — Siddharth Saminathan].

Important changes
*   **Shift from Hardcoded Normalizer**: The current hardcoded normalization approach needs to be replaced with a generic, agent-based solution that can dynamically identify and label patterns in transcripts [17 August 2026, Page 1 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Ingestion Pipeline Change for Ganesh**: Ganesh's ingestion pipeline will change from reading directly from documents to reading from the DB after the system design is complete and the normalization layer is deployed as a service [17 August 2026, Page 11-13 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **RAG Pipeline Refactoring**: The existing RAG pipeline code needs to be refactored into distinct, modular Python files and wrapped as FastAPI services for deployment, ensuring reusability and clear system boundaries [17 August 2026, Page 10-11 — Siddharth Saminathan].

What you need to know or do
As the System Owner, your immediate focus is on two main areas:
1.  **Team Intelligence Agent Refinement**: You need to redefine the capabilities of your Team Intelligence Agent, ensuring it can infer and evaluate, not just retrieve. This involves locking its persona, setting clear rules, and building out the mentor and manager agents with proper tool calls and defined roles. You also need to develop a generic normalizer for transcripts and evaluate its performance.
2.  **Knowledge Base Design**: Begin designing the knowledge base by creating a V1 version, including a JSON schema for the "training profile" that captures key information about team members (name, thinking style, tasks, evaluations). You must also decide how the LLM will be prompted to extract this information.
3.  **GitHub Integration**: Configure your agent to connect to GitHub MCP using tokens from all team members to access code and information.
4.  **Presentation Preparation**: Be ready to present your working mentor and manager agents, along with the detailed design of your knowledge base, including its components and underlying technologies.
